selection: Five selected large Bay-serving direct-service nonprofits; not an exhaustive largest-five ranking and not an impact ranking.

rows.name: Second Harvest of Silicon Valley
rows.program: Food sourcing and distribution through community partners.
rows.next: Separate additional grocery-distribution capacity from warehouse construction, reserves and replacement of existing funding.

rows.name: San Francisco–Marin Food Bank
rows.program: Pantries, home-delivered groceries and agency distribution.
rows.next: Extend our Community Markets program model with an actual expansion budget; do not apply it to the entire organization.

rows.name: Food Bank of Contra Costa and Solano
rows.geography: Contra Costa and Solano, plus wider distribution
rows.program: Food distribution, CalFresh assistance and targeted food programs.
rows.next: Test a local food-pharmacy or underserved distribution program. Its $51.7M NOR/Cluster and other-food-bank expense includes wider Northern California/Nevada distribution.

rows.name: Alameda County Community Food Bank
rows.program: Food distribution, agency support and food-benefit outreach.
rows.next: Find whether purchased food, logistics or benefit enrollment is the marginal bottleneck, then measure additional household outcomes.

rows.name: YMCA of Greater San Francisco
rows.geography: San Francisco, San Mateo and Marin; camps extend farther
rows.program: Youth development, health, camps and human services.
rows.next: Choose a specific youth or health program and test whether subsidized places create additional participation rather than replace fees or public funding.
